decisions.reason: As a freshly launched feature that fits the firm's secure identity ecosystem, its early visibility is enough for a mature firm with some slack to keep testing market acceptance rather than exit after one year.
The identity-bound wallet is closely aligned with the firm's payments-and-identity strategy, so absent clear signs of underperformance management would keep it while enterprise adoption unfolds.

Although still early and niche, the NFC login authenticator complements the firm's authentication capabilities, and a behavioral-theory firm would typically allow more time before dropping such a strategically related security product.
A secure payment and wallet framework sits near the core of the firm's super-app platform proposition and its stronger presentation suggests enough promise to retain it.
This product directly embodies the firm's stated direction toward secure multi-service platforms, so management would keep backing it even if initial results are still uncertain.
The application shielding library builds on the firm's long-standing security expertise and dedicated market presentation, making it a natural product to continue.
